KnowledgeArticle.Title: Traffic or Bicycle Signal Complaint or Request
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report a problem with an existing traffic or bicycle signal. Request a new traffic or bicycle signal.

Section.Name: 911 Traffic or Bicycle Signal Complaint or Request
Section.Content:
Call 911
Call 911 to report:
  • Signal problems causing dangerous traffic conditions
  • Signals stuck on steady green in all directions
  • Downed power lines

    Need something else?

    • Pedestrian Signal Complaint or Request to report a problem with an existing pedestrian signal or to request a new pedestrian signal
    • Electrical Complaint to report stray voltage
    • Graffiti to report graffiti impacting the visibility or operation of a traffic or bicycle signal

    You can report a problem with a traffic or bicycle signal.

    You can also request a timing review of an existing traffic or bicycle signal or request a new traffic signal.

    Learn more about traffic signals.

Section.Name: Report a Traffic or Bicycle Signal Problem
Section.Content:
You can report a traffic or bicycle signal that:

  • Is missing or damaged
  • Has burned out lights
  • Is leaning, hanging, or knocked-over poles and signals
  • Has wires outside the base or open electrical control boxes
  • Is blocked by signs, sneakers, or other hanging objects
  • Is changing out of sequence or stuck on one color
  • Is facing the wrong direction

Complaints can be made by phone only. Call 311 or 212-NEW-YORK (212-639-9675) to report the problem.

What Happens Next

Department of Transportation (DOT) contractors maintain traffic and bicycle signals in each borough.

Repairs are scheduled based on the urgency of the problem:

  • Fallen signal poles are addressed within 2 hours.
  • Exposed wiring or open electrical control boxes are addressed within 12 hours.
  • Priority issues such as problems with timing, outages, and hanging signals are addressed within 48 hours.
  • General maintenance issues are addressed within 30 days.
  • The response time for long-term construction issues varies depending on the project.

Section.Name: Check Repair Status
Section.Content:
You need your work order number to check the status of a signal repair request filed with the Department of Transportation (DOT).

Online

Check the status of a traffic signal service request.

By Phone

Call 311 or 212-NEW-YORK (212-639-9675) for help.

Section.Name: Request a Timing Review
Section.Content:
If there is a non-emergency problem with a signal's timing, you can request a timing review.

Online

Contact the Department of Transportation.

By Mail

Mail your request to:

Department of Transportation Commissioner
55 Water Street, 9th Floor
New York, NY 99999

By Phone

Call 311 or 212-NEW-YORK (212-639-9675) for help.

Section.Name: Request a New Traffic or Bicycle Signal
Section.Content:
You can submit a request for a new traffic or bicycle signal to the Department of Transportation (DOT). You must specify the type of signal in your request.

Online

Contact the Department of Transportation.

By Mail

Mail your request to:

Department of Transportation Commissioner
55 Water Street, 9th Floor
New York, NY 99999
